cars.specification_market: Original Neue Klasse four-door sporting-road saloon family, represented by the 1964 BMW 1800 TI standard road model in FIA recognition form 1286 and BMW's 2011 history. Group the 1500/1600/1800/2000 four-door programme, TI, TI/SA/TISA, tilux, tii, years and related sporting versions once. Existing 02 Series 2002 turbo is the separate later compact two-door model series; component sharing does not create a second name for the same programme. Selected engine is 1773 cc, 110 PS DIN and 9.5:1 with Solex carburettors, not 130 PS/10.5:1 Weber TI/SA or later 1766-cc 1800. Base Getrag four-speed column is selected; optional five-speed, alternative ratios, overbore allowances, 105-L tank and limited-slip equipment are not standardised. No sump capacity, torque, mass, seating count, rear anti-roll-bar standard fitment or race-car performance imported where reference scope or accounts differ.
cars.summary: The Neue Klasse 1800 TI helped establish BMW's sporting-saloon identity, combining a practical four-door production body with a tuned twin-carburettor engine and a close-ratio gearbox. Its successful touring-car competition programme and lasting historic-racing relevance are documented alongside the road model. Count the original Neue Klasse saloon programme once; do not transfer competition tuning or later TI/SA equipment into the standard road reference.

sources.title: BMW 1800 TI — original 1964 FIA/CSI recognition form 1286, initial base sheets
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer production-recognition form preserved by FIA
sources.notes: Downloaded 13-page scanned PDF. First eight PDF pages, indices 0-7, individually rendered and inspected; these contain all initial printed sheets 1-8 in scan order 1,2,3,6,7,8,4,5. Later extension pages not reviewed or imported. Seventeen attributes map to unambiguous initial base fields. Engine sheet shows 110 PS DIN at 5800 rpm, 1773 cc and alternative 9.5/10.5 compression; BMW source 1 resolves the selected road compression and Solex carburettors. Base Getrag four-speed column is separate from optional five-speed and ratios. Larger bore is an allowance, not selected displacement. Optional tank/LSD/rear anti-roll bar are not assumed standard; sump, torque, weight and seating ambiguities are omitted.

sources.title: The fresh face of BMW: 50 years of BMW New Class — 30 March 2011, printed pp. 14-17
sources.notes: Web PDF text read in opening historical context and relevant New Class/1800 TI/TISA/competition sections, not all 22 pages. Two technical attributes map to the explicitly identified road-trim 1800 TI paragraph on printed p.14: 9.5:1 compression and two Solex twin-barrel carburettors. Production road car is distinguished from TI/SA, later 2000 and racing versions. 1964 Hahne competition results provide programme context, not standard road-car performance. Local HTTP download returned HTML and web screenshot calls exposed no viewable image; no local PDF or visual-page review is claimed. Sump and rear anti-roll-bar accounts differ from FIA base sheets and are not imported.

facts.title: Touring-car success belongs to the competition programme
facts.explanation: BMW's history records Hubert Hahne winning 14 of 16 races and the German circuit title in 1964, along with a Nurburgring touring-car endurance win. These explain the 1800 TI programme's significance; competition tuning and results are not standard road-car specifications or achievements of each individual example.
